newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi signs deal with Norwegian firm.
newsitem.headline: Sappi signs deal with Norwegian firm.

text.p: South African pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd said on Sunday that it had signed a deal with Norway's Borregaard to establish a 100 million rand lignosulphonate plant.

The plant, which will have an initial capacity of 55,000 tons a year, will be sited at Sappi Saiccor in Kwa-Zulu Natal. It is scheduled for start-up in the second half of 1998 and will be the largest lignosulphonate operation in the southern hemisphere.

The world market for lignosulphonate, which goes to make a range of proucts from textiles to ceramics, is currently 1.1 million tons a year. The plant is expected to expand its capacity to tap into this growing international market, Sappi said.
Most of the plant's production will be exported and should generate around 15 million rand a year in foreign exchange earnings.
Borregaard is a major producer of lignin-based products and has 11 production units in Europe, America and Asia. It is a member of the Orkla group.

The lignin for the plant will be extracted from the wood pulp used at Sappi's normal mill operations. The firm said this would help reduce ocean colour and foam characteristics of effluent from its Umkomaas mill by 8-10 percent.
